items.stem: Priya invests $500 for 3 years at a rate of 4% per year simple interest.

parts.t: Calculate the interest Priya receives.

sols: Simple interest is worked out on the original $500 every year.
ms:
M1 for 500 × 4 × 3⁄100 oe or 20 seen
A1 cao

items.stem: Daniel invests $2000 for 2 years at a rate of 3% per year compound interest.

parts.t: Calculate the value of his investment at the end of the 2 years.
Write down the interest he receives.

sols: Increasing by 3% means multiplying by 1.03 each year.
one factor of 1.03 for each year
this is more than the $120 that simple interest would give

items.stem:
Kofi invests $800 at a rate of r% per year simple interest.
After 5 years the total interest is $140.

parts.t: Find the value of r.
Calculate the total value of Kofi’s investment after 8 years.

items.stem: Mrs Okafor invests $4500 for 5 years at a rate of 2.8% per year compound interest.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of the investment at the end of the 5 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Calculate the total interest she receives, correct to the nearest dollar.

sols: Each year the investment is multiplied by 1 + <sup>2.8</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> = 1.028.
compare: simple interest would have given only $630
ms:
M1 for 1.028 seen as a multiplier
M1 for 4500 × 1.0285 oe
A1 cao

B1
FT their value − 4500, rounded to the nearest dollar

items.stem:
A car is bought for $18 000.
Its value decreases by 15% of its value at the start of each year.

parts.t: Calculate the value of the car after 3 years.
Work out the loss in value of the car over the 3 years.

Calculate the overall percentage decrease in the value of the car.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: A decrease of 15% means multiplying by 1 − 0.15 = 0.85 each year.
not 45%: each year’s 15% is taken from a smaller amount
ms:
B1
FT, accept 38.5875 or better rounded to 3 s.f.

items.stem:
Nadia and Tomas each invest $3000 for 4 years.
Nadia’s account pays 5% per year simple interest.
Tomas’s account pays 5% per year compound interest.

parts.t: Calculate the value of Nadia’s investment after 4 years.

Calculate the value of Tomas’s investment after 4 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Work out how much more Tomas has than Nadia after 4 years.

sols: Compound interest multiplies by 1.05 each year.
compound interest also earns interest on the interest already added

items.stem:
The population of a town is 24 000.
The population increases at a rate of 3.2% per year.

parts.t:
Calculate the population after 6 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
Find the least number of complete years after which the population is greater than 30 000.

sols: An increase of 3.2% per year means multiplying by 1.032 each year.
correct to the nearest whole number
After 7 years: 24 000 × 1.032<sup>7</sup> = 29 920.5…, which is still less than 30 000.
After 8 years: 24 000 × 1.032<sup>8</sup> = 30 878.0…, which is greater than 30 000.
ms:
M1 for a correct trial with n = 7 or n = 8 (29 920 or 30 878 seen)
A1 cao

items.stem:

After 2 years her investment is worth $5512.50.

parts.t: Calculate the amount of money Elena invested.
Calculate the value of her investment 3 years after that, giving your answer correct to the nearest cent.

sols: divide, because we are working backwards

items.stem: Layla invests $6000 at a rate of 4.5% per year compound interest.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of her investment after 4 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Find the least number of complete years after which the value of her investment is greater than $9000.

sols: The multiplier for one year is 1 + <sup>4.5</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> = 1.045.
ms:
M1 for 6000 × 1.045n > 9000 oe
M1 for both trials, 8916.57 and 9317.82 (or 1.045n > 1.5 with a correct trial)
A1 cao, not 9

items.stem:
Hassan invests $12 000 in account A, which pays compound interest at a rate of r% per year.
After 5 years the value of this investment is $15 315.38.

Account B pays simple interest at a rate of 4.6% per year.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of r.
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
Calculate the value of $12 000 invested in account B for 5 years.
Work out how much more account A gives than account B over the 5 years.

sols: Let the yearly multiplier be k, so 12 000 × k5 = 15 315.38.
take the 5th root of the multiplier
The multiplier 1.05 means an increase of 0.05 = 5%.
Simple interest for one year = 4.6% of 12 000 = $552.
ms:
M1 for 15315.38 ÷ 12000 (= 1.27628…)
M1 for 5√their 1.27628… oe
A1 cao, accept 5
